title: Value group of a separably closed valued field is divisible
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed] [def-weil-field], and let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation subring with fraction field $K$: for every $x\in K^\times$, either $x\in V$ or $x^{-1}\in V$. Write $\Gamma=K^\times/V^\times$ for its value group, where $V^\times=\{u\in V\setminus\{0\}:u^{-1}\in V\}$. Then $\Gamma$ is divisible: for every $\gamma\in\Gamma$ and every integer $n\geq1$ there is $\delta\in\Gamma$ with $n\delta=\gamma$ (equivalently, $\delta^n=\gamma$ multiplicatively).

proof.text: Put $U=V^\times$. Products and inverses show that $U$ is a subgroup of $K^\times$. On $\Gamma=K^\times/U$ define $v(a)\le v(b)$ iff $b/a\in V$. This is independent of representatives because multiplying by units preserves membership in $V$. Reflexivity and transitivity use $1\in V$ and closure under products; antisymmetry follows because both ratios in $V$ mean their ratio is a unit. The inverse alternative gives totality, and cancelling a common factor gives translation invariance. Hence this is an ordered abelian group, $v(ab)=v(a)+v(b)$, $v(-a)=v(a)$ since $-1\in U$, and $v(a)\ge0$ iff $a\in V$. It suffices to find $b\in K^\times$ with $n v(b)=v(a)$ for every $a\in K^\times$ and $n\ge1$.

proof.text: Here is the unequal-value calculation directly from the subring definition. If $x,y,x+y$ are nonzero and $v(x)\le v(y)$, then $y/x\in V$ and $(x+y)/x=1+y/x\in V$, so $v(x+y)\ge v(x)$; exchanging $x,y$ proves $v(x+y)\ge\min(v(x),v(y))$ whenever the sum is nonzero. Now suppose $v(r)<v(s)$. Then $r+s\ne0$, since $s=-r$ would imply equal values. The inequality gives $v(r+s)\ge v(r)$. If this inequality were strict, apply the same inequality to $(r+s)+(-s)=r$: both summands have value strictly greater than $v(r)$, a contradiction. Thus $v(r+s)=v(r)$; the opposite strict order follows by exchanging the terms. This proves the needed identity for arbitrary rank without a discrete-valuation assumption.

proof.text: Let $p=\operatorname{char}K$. If $p=0$, the image of every positive integer $n$ in $K$ is nonzero, so [lem-trf-separably-closed-prime-to-char-root] gives $b^n=a$ and hence $n v(b)=v(a)$. If $p>0$, write $n=p^r m$ with $r\ge0$ and $p\nmid m$. The image of $m$ in $K$ is then nonzero, so the prime-to-characteristic factor can be extracted by [lem-trf-separably-closed-prime-to-char-root] once a $p^r$-th value root has been obtained.

proof.text: Since every $a\in K^\times$ and every $n\ge1$ admit $b$ with $n v(b)=v(a)$, every class in $\Gamma$ has an $n$-th root. Returning to multiplicative notation, this says that for each $\gamma\in\Gamma$ there is $\delta\in\Gamma$ with $\delta^n=\gamma$, so $\Gamma$ is divisible.
